reference_observations.observed_value: The bracelet is composed of large individually distinctive stone- or fossil-like elements rather than a uniform repeated bead strand; each major unit differs in shape, pattern, translucency and color.
One oversized spiral fossil-like element is the dominant visual focal and is substantially larger and more irregular than the surrounding units.
The design uses a clear hierarchy of one oversized hero element, several large rounded or irregular secondary elements, and very small dark spacer beads between them.
Rounded spheres, faceted or polygonal forms, barrel-like forms, irregular stone-like chunks and the spiral focal coexist in the same bracelet.
The palette mixes mossy green, ochre, amber-brown, cream, smoky gray, muted blue-gray and black details, producing an earthy coastal-geological impression without a single dominant bright color.
Visible surfaces range from translucent and glossy to cloudy, patterned, banded and fossil-like, making internal and surface variation a major part of the composition.
Small glossy black spacer beads separate many of the large heterogeneous units, providing a repeated visual punctuation and preventing adjacent complex elements from visually merging.

The composition appears to treat each large element as an individual collected fragment, with cohesion coming from the restrained earth-toned palette and repeated black spacers rather than from matching shapes.

The user's concept name '白垩纪的海岸碎片' fits the visual strategy of assembling irregular, fossil-like, sedimentary-looking and sea-toned fragments into one bracelet; this is a design-narrative interpretation, not a geological provenance claim.
The product is photographed on a warm off-white background with strong negative space, black serif branding and minimal editorial typography.
One source image annotates individual components with seller-provided material names and nominal sizes around the bracelet, emphasizing the uniqueness of each large unit.

Another source image labels the shown orientation as 'side A', indicating that the design is intended to be viewed as a deliberately arranged multi-sided composition rather than an interchangeable uniform strand.
